title: Hanlon's razor
src: Attributed to Robert J. Hanlon, Murphy's Law Book Two, 1980
idea: Never attribute to malice what carelessness, stress, or a bad day can explain.
apply: When someone slights you, write the most boring explanation first. Then ask one calm question before reacting.
remind: Assume the mistake first. Ask before you accuse.
who: Nina, waiting on a reply from a coworker.

msgs.x: Can you send the report by Tuesday?

scenes.nar: Nina asks her coworker Omar for a report by Tuesday. It is Thursday, and he still has not answered.

msgs.x: He is ignoring me on purpose.

scenes.nar: Her first thought is that he is ignoring her on purpose. She starts typing an angry reply.

msgs.x: Maybe he is buried and forgot.
Hey Omar, did my report request get buried? Just need it by Monday.

scenes.nar: Then she tries the boring explanation. He is probably swamped and forgot. So she sends one friendly question instead.

msgs.x: Sorry!! Totally buried. Sending it now.

scenes.nar: Omar answers within minutes. The message had simply been lost under a pile of others.
